extraction.name: OpenThoughts3-1.2M
extraction.description: OpenThoughts3-1.2M is a 1.2 million example supervised fine-tuning dataset for training reasoning models, containing math, code, and science question-response pairs. Responses are generated using QwQ-32B as a teacher model, with questions sourced and filtered through a systematic pipeline involving question sourcing, mixing, filtering, deduplication, and multiple answer sampling.
extraction.creator: Etash Guha; Ryan Marten; Sedrick Keh; Negin Raoof; Georgios Smymis; Hritik Bansal; Marianna Nezhurina; Jean Mercat; Trung Vu; Zayne Sprague; Ashima Suvama; Benjamin Feuer; Liangyu Chen; Zaid Khan; Eric Frankel; Sachin Grover; Caroline Choi; Niklas Muennighoff; Shiye Su; Wanjia Zhao; John Yang; Shreyas Pimpalgaonkar; Kartik Sharma; Charlie Cheng-Jie Ji; Yichuan Deng; Sarah Pratt; Vivek Ramanujan; Jon Saad-Falcon; Jeffrey Li; Achal Dave; Alon Albalak; Kushal Arora; Blake Wulfe; Chinmay Hegde; Greg Durrett; Sewoong Oh; Mohit Bansal; Saadia Gabriel; Aditya Grover; Kai-Wei Chang; Vaishaal Shankar; Aaron Gokaslan; Mike A. extraction.citeAs: Etash Guha, Ryan Marten, Sedrick Keh, Negin Raoof, Georgios Smymis, et al. Data Recipes for Reasoning Models. arXiv:2506.04178, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by sourcing questions from existing public datasets, online forums (e.g., StackExchange, CodeForces), competition problem sets, and organic chemistry PDFs, as well as generating synthetic and semi-synthetic questions using LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, Gemini) from seed texts such as CommonCrawl, FineWeb, Wikipedia, and textbooks. Answers (reasoning traces) were generated by querying teacher models (primarily DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ-32B) for each question, with multiple answers sampled per question.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Web Scraping; Software Collection; Manual Human Curator; User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source questions drawn from: StackExchange forums (CodeGolf, Physics, Biology, StackOverflow), OpenCodeReasoning, KodCode-V1, NuminaMath-1.5, OpenMath-2-Math, AutoMathText, MathPile, DeepMath-103K, CodeForces, TACO, Apps, CodeContests, CodeFeedback, OpenR1-Math, organic chemistry PDFs (SCP-116K and textbooks), Wikipedia science articles, FineWeb, CommonCrawl (DCLM-RefinedWeb), arXiv abstracts, and various other Hugging Face datasets. Reasoning traces (answers) generated by DeepSeek-R1 and QwQ-32B teacher models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were annotated (answered) by teacher LLM models (primarily QwQ-32B in the final pipeline, DeepSeek-R1 in earlier stages) to generate reasoning traces and answers. Multiple answers per question were sampled (up to 16x). Question filtering used GPT-4o-mini or GPT-4.1-mini/nano to assess difficulty or response length. Answer filtering experiments used GPT-4o-mini for verification, majority consensus, and other quality checks. For the legal reasoning appendix, DeepSeek-R1 annotated examples 5x independently with majority vote or expert-label verification.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Answer filtering experiments explored majority consensus (GPT-4o-mini selects indices of responses agreeing with the majority answer), GPT verification (GPT-4o-mini judges correctness), FastText classifiers, length-based selection, and random filtering. The main finding was that no filtering strategy outperformed using all samples, so no answer filtering was applied in the final pipeline. For the legal reasoning experiment, majority vote over 5 R1 annotations was used to verify answers.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: QwQ-32B; DeepSeek-R1; GPT-4o-mini; GPT-4.1-mini; GPT-4.1-nano; Phi-4-Reasoning-Plus; Claude 3.7 (with thinking mode); gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite-preview-02-05; FastText; OpenAI text-embedding-3-large
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The work did not explore datasets for reinforcement learning; within the SFT realm, staged SFT or curriculum learning were not explored; distilled reasoning models still suffer from generalization deficits as evident from strong performance fluctuations across natural problem and solution structure preserving variations in problem templates; supervised fine-tuning on reasoning inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of Qwen2.5 models, with OpenThinker3-7B trained without any explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Supervised fine-tuning on reasoning inadvertently degrades the pre-existing safety alignment of Qwen2.5 models, consistent with prior findings; OpenThinker3-7B reaches the highest harmfulness score (55.5 on Harmbench) and was trained without any explicit safety-tuning or alignment-focused data; the authors note a clear trade-off between reasoning capabilities and safety, and state that future work would benefit from incorporating safety-specific datasets to mitigate these risks while preserving strong reasoning capabilities
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) reasoning models in math, code, and science domains; benchmarking and comparing data curation strategies for reasoning model development
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset pipeline includes several post-collection manipulations: (1) Sampling multiple answers per question (1×, 4×, or 16×) from teacher models to increase answer diversity and dataset scale; (2) Exact and fuzzy deduplication of questions using Normalized Indel similarity (LCS-based) to reduce repetition; (3) Mixing questions from top-performing sources (top 1, 2, 4, 8, or 16 sources) to form the final dataset composition; (4) The final OpenThoughts3-1.2M pipeline uses 16× answer sampling per question, exact deduplication for math and science, and no deduplication for code.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The pipeline includes the following preprocessing steps: (1) Question filtering using LLM-based methods including difficulty-based selection (GPT-4o-mini rates questions 1-10) and response length filtering (GPT-4.1-mini or GPT-4.1-nano generates responses and selects questions with longest outputs); classical methods such as FastText classifiers and embedding-based selection were also tested but underperformed LLM-based methods. (2) Answer filtering experiments including removing non-English answers, removing long paragraphs, majority consensus selection, GPT verification, and shortest/longest answer selection; however, no answer filtering strategy was adopted in the final pipeline as none outperformed the no-filtering baseline. (3) Decontamination against evaluation benchmarks using two methods: Normalized Indel similarity (LCS-based, 75% threshold) and N-gram overlap (N=13, using Qwen2-7B-Instruct tokenizer); samples flagged by either method are discarded. (4) For the organic chemistry PDF pipeline, Gemini was used for OCR text extraction, GPT-4o-mini extracted questions and answers, refined questions, and filtered out non-science/math/code questions using structured decoding.
